comparisons.peer_topic: AOCI Composition and Amortization for HTM Securities
comparisons.peer_summary: Net unrealized losses in AOCI for HTM securities relate to previous AFS transfers and fair value hedge adjustments, including non-credit fair value changes on impaired securities, and are amortized as a yield adjustment consistent with accretion of differences between carrying value and par value.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Citigroup disclose that unrealized losses in Accumulated Other Comprehensive Income (AOCI) relate to securities previously classified as Available-for-Sale (AFS) that were transferred to Held-to-Maturity (HTM). JPM reports specific after-tax net unamortized unrealized loss amounts of $(651) million for 2024 related to these transfers, while Citigroup describes the composition of this AOCI balance for HTM securities, noting it primarily relates to such transfers and is amortized as a yield adjustment.

The net unrealized losses classified in AOCI for HTM debt securities primarily relate to debt securities previously classified as AFS that were transferred to HTM, and include any cumulative fair value hedge adjustments.
